title: Security & hosting options — Greenfall Apps discovery

Agreed next steps: send SOC2/ISO artifacts, share network diagram and deployment checklist, schedule technical deep dive for private deployment POC.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-15 15:00 PDT
Duration: 41 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Evan Brooks (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO - Greenfall), Tom Alvarez (Head of Security - Greenfall), Liam O'Neill (Principal Eng - Greenfall)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): intake call on security, hosting options, KMS/ BYOK questions, SSO and audit log retention.

[00:00:05] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm maya, account exec at Redwood. Evan is our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:14] Priya Nair: Hi, i'm priya, CTO at Greenfall. Thanks. We really want to understand the security tradeoffs — we're deciding between hosted, reserved/dedicated, or a private/VPC deployment.
[00:00:25] Tom Alvarez: Tom here, i'm head of security. Main items for me: SOC2 scope, encryption at rest keys, BYOK options, and audit log retention.
[00:00:33] Evan Brooks: Great — we'll walk through each. Quick note, apologies if transcription mangles acronyms, sometimes K M S comes through odd.
[00:00:40] Liam O'Neill: Also curious about latency and egress cost implications if we go private.

[00:01:05] Maya Chen: High level: hosted is fastest to get started — our hosted API with token-level monitoring. Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs + isolation in our tenancy. Private is a VPC/on-prem control plane with customer-managed network and optional BYOK.
[00:01:25] Priya Nair: For compliance, our vertical requires SOC2 type II and ISO 27001 evidence. Do you have those?
[00:01:35] Maya Chen: Yes. We can share SOC2 Type II report and our ISO 27001 attestation. Evan, is there a note about redwood's scope?
[00:01:44] Evan Brooks: Right — our SOC2 covers the hosted control plane and certain operational practices; I'll pull the most recent bridge letter and the scope doc. For private deployments the scope shifts, and we provide a different compliance pack.
[00:02:02] Tom Alvarez: When you say scope shifts, do you mean our auditors will expect us to show controls in our VPC instead of Redwood-managed infra?
[00:02:09] Evan Brooks: Exactly — with Private you manage the customer VPC and KMS; Redwood provides a control plane but you hold network controls. We'll document which controls remain with you vs Redwood in the shared responsibility matrix.

[00:02:40] Priya Nair: Encryption — we need BYOK and HSM-backed keys. Is that supported in hosted?
[00:02:48] Maya Chen: Hosted supports customer-managed keys in some regions via BYOK integrated with our KMS layer; for full HSM-backed keys we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can bring your own HSM or integrate with your cloud KMS/HSM.
[00:03:05] Tom Alvarez: Is there a latency hit when using BYOK?
[00:03:10] Evan Brooks: Minimal for normal crypto operations; the bigger impact is key wrapping/unwrapping at token issuance time. For high-throughput inference we cache decrypted keys in a secure enclave with strict TTLs to reduce per-request overhead — we can show numbers in the POC.

[00:03:45] Liam O'Neill: About RBAC: we need role separation and audit logs for admin actions. Can Redwood surface per-user actions and admin role changes?
[00:03:55] Maya Chen: Yes — our Console exposes RBAC roles and audit trails. In hosted you'll get our standard roles; for enterprise Dedicated/Private we support custom role mappings and SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning.
[00:04:12] Tom Alvarez: What about retention of logs — like API request traces, prompts, and outputs? We have legal needs to keep certain logs for 7 years for a regulated product.
[00:04:23] Evan Brooks: By default we retain operational logs for 13 months, audit logs for X months (note: placeholder), but we can configure extended retention as an add-on for enterprise customers. Prompt/response retention is configurable and can be redacted or disabled. For 7-year retention we'd likely route logs to your long-term storage (S3 with lifecycle policies) via our secure forwarding hooks.
[00:04:52] Tom Alvarez: Can logs be exported in an encrypted format and stored behind our KMS?
[00:04:58] Evan Brooks: Yes — you can push logs to your own account or have us ship encrypted blobs to your storage using your KMS keys. That's common for customers with long-term retention rules.

[00:05:22] Priya Nair: SSO — we use Okta and enforce SAML 2.0 with SCIM for provisioning. Do you support SCIM and fine-grained claims?
[00:05:31] Maya Chen: Yes — SAML + SCIM provisioning is supported; we map SCIM groups to RBAC roles. For advanced claims you can configure attribute mappings. We'll provide the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints.
[00:05:48] Liam O'Neill: Do you support MFA enforced by our IdP?
[00:05:51] Evan Brooks: MFA is enforced at the IdP level — if your IdP requires MFA, that policy applies to Redwood logins via SAML.

[00:06:10] Tom Alvarez: Audit logs again — are there immutable logs for admin activity? For exam- ple, can we show tamper-proof records for config changes?
[00:06:20] Evan Brooks: We can provide append-only audit logs with cryptographic checksums or ship them to your write-once storage. We'll include specifics in the compliance pack.

[00:06:50] Priya Nair: Data residency — we need all inference to run in eu-west-1 for EU customers. How do you handle region pinning?
[00:06:58] Maya Chen: You can pin model routing to region and region-specific model variants. Dedicated pools can be provisioned in eu-west-1; Private obviously runs in your region. For hosted, we have EU clusters we can route to by policy.

[00:07:24] Liam O'Neill: About the model artifacts — will the raw model weights be stored on Redwood-managed infra in hosted? We need to avoid weights leaving our control for certain models.
[00:07:32] Evan Brooks: In hosted, model binaries are managed by Redwood. For workloads that require you to control model artifacts, Private or Dedicated where you host weights in your environment or under a customer-managed tenancy is recommended.

[00:07:55] Tom Alvarez: Do you offer contract language for data processing agreements (DPA) with specific security commitments?
[00:08:02] Maya Chen: Yes — standard DPA is available; for enterprise we can negotiate additional compliance clauses. I'll attach our DPA and a sample contract addendum.

[00:08:25] Priya Nair: Timeline — we want to pilot in prod-like environment within 6 weeks. realistic?
[00:08:33] Evan Brooks: For a hosted pilot it's immediate. For a Dedicated reserved pool onboarding is typically 2–4 weeks depending on quota. Private/PVX on-prem can be 4–8 weeks depending on networking and HSM provisioning. For a 6-week goal, Dedicated or a Private with prepared infra could work.

[00:09:05] Liam O'Neill: For benchmarks: we need latency at p95 under 300ms for short prompts and throughput estimates. Can you run sample workloads?
[00:09:14] Evan Brooks: Yes — we can run a benchmark with your sample prompts. We'll want a test token set and target sequence lengths. We'll include cost per 1k tokens at different quantization levels and batch configs.

[00:09:45] Tom Alvarez: Is there a way to toggle prompt logging per environment? We want staging to log full prompts but prod to redact.
[00:09:53] Maya Chen: We have per-route logging controls and environment flags. You can disable prompt capture on prod routes and enable it in staging. Redaction helpers also available.

[00:10:18] Priya Nair: Ok. A few specific questions from legal: can you support subprocessor lists and notify us for changes?
[00:10:27] Maya Chen: We maintain a subprocessors registry and provide notification windows for changes. We'll include the current list and the change / approval process.

[00:10:45] Liam O'Neill: Are there any known limitations in your RBAC mapping when integrating with complex orgs (multiple domains/nested groups)?
[00:10:53] Evan Brooks: We support nested group mappings via SCIM group attributes and can do custom role import for complex hierarchies. For extremely custom setups we recommend a Dedicated or Private deployment where you control the IdP mappings more tightly.

[00:11:20] Priya Nair: Costs — we will evaluate unit economics. For security it's fine to pay extra for guaranteed retention and BYOK. Do you have add-on pricing for retention and extended support?
[00:11:29] Maya Chen: Yes — extended retention, dedicated audit storage forwarding, and BYOK/HSM integrations are enterprise add-ons. I'll include a rough pricing sheet.

[00:11:50] Tom Alvarez: Clarify key rotation policies — for BYOK what are the rotation windows and how do you handle rotation during active sessions?
[00:11:58] Evan Brooks: Key rotation is orchestrated with minimal disruption: we support double encryption periods where old keys remain valid for a short TTL while new keys take effect. We'll describe the exact rotation protocol in the KMS appendix.

[00:12:25] Liam O'Neill: Is there penetration testing or external audit reports we can review?
[00:12:30] Maya Chen: We can share recent pentest summaries and remediation tickets; full reports may be covered by NDA — we'll provide redacted versions or an NDA if needed.

[00:12:48] Priya Nair: Anything else we should know about compliance logging?
[00:12:52] Evan Brooks: One sticky point is prompt-level logging — we treat it separately from infrastructure logs. If you need legal hold or e-discovery searchability for prompts, we'll route and index those to your own search cluster in an encrypted form.

[00:13:18] Maya Chen: Ok, quick recap: we'll send SOC2 and ISO certs, a shared responsibility matrix, network diagram for private deployment, sample DPA and subprocessors list, and a pricing/add-ons sheet. We'll also propose dates for a POC deep dive.
[00:13:33] Priya Nair: Sounds good — thanks. Also note we need a named security contact for Redwood for our vendor inventory.
[00:13:40] Maya Chen: That'll be Tom Peters (Redwood Security Liaison) — i'll include contact in the follow-up.

[00:13:55] Tom Alvarez: One last question — can you support egress restrictions so model outputs never leave EU?
[00:14:03] Evan Brooks: Yes — with region pinned routing and Dedicated/Private deployments you can ensure inference executes and data remains in the EU. We'll document network flow and routing policies.

[00:14:22] Priya Nair: Great. Let's schedule the POC deep dive. preferred days next week are tues/thurs mornings.
[00:14:30] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll follow up with calendar invites.

[00:14:40] (crosstalk)
[00:14:45] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll get the artifacts over tomorrow and Evan will prep the config doc.
[00:14:52] Priya Nair: Thank you.
[00:14:54] Tom Alvarez: Thanks.

(End of meeting)
